label: r4c1
name: shift gate + entropy 0.05
hypothesis: Same as r3c3, but the entropy coefficient rises from 0.03 to the maximum, 0.05. Raising it from 0.01 to 0.03 lifted the weak seed from collapse to 0.23 (full stack) and to 0.61 (gate). More entropy should delay the early collapse onto DONE further, so the weak seed reaches seed 0's level of about 0.84. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above 0.72, or if seed 0 falls clearly below 0.8.
last_analysis: Every model that learned anything uses some way of undoing the target shift: a stack of shifted copies or a learned shift gate. Without it, the agent quickly learns to choose DONE before placing anything. Seed 0 seems to top out at about 0.84 under any reasonable setup. Seed 1 decides the mean: across trials it scored 0.31, 0.60, 0, 0, 0, 0.23, 0.08 and 0.61. The best result, r3c3 (0.72), is the shared shift gate plus entropy 0.03, the only setup where seed 1 got above 0.6. Its training success was still rising at the end. Things that hurt stability: 64 envs (both seeds collapsed) and 2 PPO epochs (one seed collapsed). With 128 envs both seeds survived. The useful moves are those that make seed 1 align faster or collapse later. All three candidates keep r3c3 and change one thing: a stronger entropy bonus, more parallel worlds per update at the same number of updates, or more gate mixtures.
